reports_for_other_owners: No new defects. The accepted expansive study still says 'the seven orations of this Mass' in sections/05-appointed-texts.tex and sections/90-synthesis.tex although the leaf prints six (five feast orations plus the commemorated Collect); already reported by derive-study-3 and derive-synthesis-0, and remains with the study's owner. The homily avoids the count ('the Collect', 'the prayers of this Mass') and was verified to contain no 'seven' count.

The homily's spoken body runs about 1,445 words (some 11.1-12.0 minutes at 120-130 words per minute by arithmetic alone); it has not been delivered aloud or timed, and any future re-voicing should keep the revision timestamp, the note's length paragraph and the production-audit entry in step.
summary: Wrote the All Saints homily 'The Way the Saints Walked' (homily.tex plus its two manifest-declared components): a 1,445-word spoken body, ready to read aloud to an adult parish assembly at the Mass of All Saints said on Sunday 1 November 2026, taking its spine from the accepted study's second interpretation (Augustine's ordered way and Chrysostom's golden chain) and borrowing from the first (Bede's definite number signifying the innumerable multitude, Augustine's 'mass of the saints') and the third (Augustine's objector, Basil's perfect good, Aquinas's nourisher-and-physician, Schuster's hands sentence). The speech joins the Gospel to the Introit, Lesson, Alleluia, Gradual, Offertory, Secret, Communion and Postcommunion, hears the commemorated Sunday's Collect as the prayer of the first step, and ends at the Communion's three beatitudes on 'the clean of heart shall see God'; the note on sources and delivery records audience, length and pace, the relation to the study's three interpretations, the route of every quoted text, and the exact loci. All component-contract and content-preflight gates pass; the 4-page proof PDF was inspected at raster resolution page by page.
